sections.question: Can tourists buy weed in Los Angeles?
sections.short: Yes, if you are 21 or older and show a valid ID, such as a driver’s license or a passport, at a store licensed by California’s Department of Cannabis Control.

points.text: In California, adults 21 and older can buy cannabis for adult use. Cities and counties may have stricter rules than the state.

Licensed retailers must confirm your age and identity with a valid ID. The Department of Cannabis Control lists a government-issued ID with a photo, such as a driver’s license, an Armed Forces ID, or a passport issued by the United States or a foreign government.
In the City of Los Angeles, a cannabis business also needs local authorization from the city before it can sell.

sections.question: How do I know a Los Angeles cannabis store is licensed?
sections.short: Look for the state license in the window and scan its QR code, or look the store up in the Department of Cannabis Control’s License Search. The City of Los Angeles also lists the stores it has authorized.

points.text: Every cannabis retailer in California must have a license from the Department of Cannabis Control. Some stores that look legitimate are not licensed and may sell products that have not been tested.
Licensed retailers display their state license in the storefront window, and you can scan its QR code to check the license’s status.
The Department’s License Search is updated daily and can be used to check a license or to find licensed retailers.

sections.question: How much weed can I have in California?
sections.short: Up to 28.5 grams of cannabis and up to 8 grams of concentrated cannabis, the same amounts the state gives as the daily limit for adult-use customers.

points.text: Adults 21 and older may possess up to 28.5 grams of non-concentrated cannabis and up to 8 grams of concentrated cannabis, under Health and Safety Code section 11362.1.
The Department of Cannabis Control gives the same amounts as the daily limit for adult-use customers: 28.5 grams of non-concentrated cannabis and 8 grams of concentrated cannabis.

sections.question: Where can you smoke weed in Los Angeles?
sections.short: On private property where the owner allows it. Not in public places such as restaurants or bars, not anywhere tobacco smoking is banned, not in a car and not on federal land.

points.text: You can use cannabis on private property, but not in public places such as restaurants or bars.
You can’t smoke cannabis anywhere tobacco smoking is illegal, or within 1,000 feet of a school, day care center or youth center while children are present.
Property owners can ban cannabis use on their property, and renters should check their rental agreement.
Under federal law, you can’t use or possess cannabis on federal lands such as national parks.

sections.question: Can I smoke weed in my Los Angeles hotel room?
sections.short: Usually not. California’s cannabis regulator says most hotels don’t allow guests to use cannabis in their rooms, so ask the front desk first.

points.text: Most hotels do not allow guests to use cannabis in their hotel room. The Department of Cannabis Control says to ask the reception desk about the hotel’s policy.
If you are staying in a vacation rental, check with the owner.

sections.question: Can I have weed in a car in Los Angeles, or drive after using it?
sections.short: Keep it in a sealed package or container, or in the trunk. An open container while driving or riding is illegal, and so is driving high.

points.text: It’s illegal to have an open container of cannabis while driving or riding in a vehicle. Cannabis in a vehicle must be in a sealed package or container, or in the trunk.
Officers can pull you over for a sobriety test.
Driving under the influence of cannabis is illegal and carries the same potential penalties as driving under the influence of alcohol.

sections.question: Can I bring weed to a national park or national forest from Los Angeles?
sections.short: No. Federal law still bans using or having cannabis on federal land, including national parks and national forests.

points.text: Under federal law, you can’t use or possess cannabis on federal lands such as national parks.

The U.S. Forest Service’s Pacific Southwest Region says that under federal law, cultivating or using cannabis on federal lands is illegal. If you come across a cannabis grow site, it says, do not enter the area.

sections.question: Can I fly home with weed from Los Angeles?
sections.short: No. California’s cannabis regulator says you can’t take cannabis across state lines, and federal law still applies at airport security.

points.text: Under federal law, you can’t take cannabis across state lines.

TSA says marijuana and some cannabis products, including some CBD oil, remain illegal under federal law unless they have no more than 0.3% THC on a dry-weight basis or are FDA-approved. Its officers don’t search for drugs, but they refer anything illegal they find to law enforcement.

sections.question: Does California accept medical cannabis cards from other states?
sections.short: No. California does not recognize other states’ medical marijuana identification cards, but visitors 21 and older can buy at adult-use stores.

points.text: California’s Department of Public Health says the state does not recognize other states’ medical marijuana identification cards.
Adults 21 and older can still buy cannabis for adult use at a licensed store.

sections.question: How much of an edible should I take?
sections.short: Start low and go slow. California’s regulator says edibles can take up to two hours to start working and up to four hours for the full effect.

points.text: Edibles can take up to two hours to begin working and up to four hours for their full effects. The Department of Cannabis Control’s advice is “Start low, go slow!”
Keep cannabis in a sealed, child-resistant package. If a child has eaten cannabis, call poison control at 1-800-222-1222.
